tasks.short: Plan and supervise pathology staff and trainees

steps.what: Find and check the actual case workload, staff availability, competencies and trainee supervision needs
inputs: Existing case workload records in the pathology information system, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
Actual staff availability and competency records
outputs: Checked planning context and unresolved staffing constraints

steps.what: Plan appropriate case work and supervision for staff, residents and visiting pathologists
inputs: Checked workload and competency context
outputs: Pathologist's actual work and supervision plan

steps.what: Capture and check the complete actual work plan and supervision responsibilities
inputs: Actual plan from s2
Verified staff and case identifiers
outputs: Final checked work plan

steps.what: Save the checked work plan in the existing shared planning record
inputs: Exact complete plan from s3
outputs: Saved work plan available in the existing team workspace

steps.what: Supervise the actual pathology work, discuss cases and provide resident or visiting-pathologist guidance
inputs: Actual work and people
Checked work plan
outputs: Active human supervision and case-specific guidance

tasks.design: Configure the existing workload view and fixed plan fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The pathologist plans responsibilities and checks the final saved plan, then supervises actual work in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding case and staff context and repeating identifiers can interrupt work planning.
tasks.enabler_now: Native workload views and forms can reduce navigation and fixed-field entry.
tasks.still_hard: Assigning appropriate responsibility and recognising supervision needs require professional judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Judge capability and provide case-specific guidance and feedback.

ambition.what: Support current work planning and supervision.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native case-workload views and planning fields can support pathology work coordination without replacing supervision or assignment judgement.

assumptions: Conditional episode with an actual shared work-plan record, not a new report after each supervision conversation or a measured duty mix.
Case and personnel owners produce existing records; pathologist retrieval, checking and actual plan capture remain in s1-s3. No free new competency assessment or normalized staffing feed.

Native features first; existing views and fields are baseline. s3 reduces fixed identifiers only; the plan decision and complete check remain human. No automatic assignment, notification or case approval.
Saving is negligible and fully retained. Any actual plan change repeats the final-version check before saving; later clinical sign-outs require their own separate clinical review.
All 100 illustrative focal effort points: gross 3 plus 1.4 equals 4.4; upkeep 1 gives net 3.4.
unknowns: Actual plan-record practice and source availability
research_questions: Which planning navigation and fixed-field entry remain manual after existing features?

already_counted.description: Workload checking, substantive work planning and retained plan capture and final review

incremental.description: Maintain existing workload view and plan fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete work plan checked in s3; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional native lookup and fixed-field saving 4.4 less upkeep 1; actual supervision and planning judgement retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform autopsies and determine causes of death

steps.what: Check actual case identity, authority, available records and readiness for the specific autopsy under established procedures
inputs: Actual case and authority records
Established procedure and actual examination conditions
Existing pathology case system, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Checked case and readiness for the specific examination or decision to stop

steps.what: Perform the actual autopsy and capture examination observations using established professional procedures
inputs: Specific case and readiness checked in s1
Actual examination material
outputs: Actual observed findings and captured examination evidence

steps.what: Integrate actual findings and case evidence to determine the cause of death and its limitations
inputs: Actual findings and observations from s2
Verified case evidence
outputs: Pathologist's cause-of-death assessment with unresolved findings marked

steps.what: Write the actual autopsy findings and cause assessment and check the complete final case record
inputs: Actual captured findings and human assessment
outputs: Complete checked autopsy record

steps.what: Save the exact checked autopsy record
inputs: Exact complete record from s4
outputs: Saved autopsy findings with actual final or pending status

tasks.design: Retain the physical examination, causal interpretation and actual report writing in the existing {OPS_SYSTEM} case process. No new automation with a supported labour reduction is established for this episode.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task depends on actual examination evidence and expert causal assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated new mechanism removes the examination, reasoning or substantive report work here.
tasks.still_hard: Cause-of-death assessment must account for the complete evidence and unresolved findings.
tasks.human_edge: Observe, integrate evidence and document the limits of the conclusion.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: autopsy examination, causal interpretation and substantive reporting require professional judgement; existing case-record tools do not alone establish new savings.

assumptions: Illustrative active-effort split, not measured baseline. Physical examination, evidence capture, causal interpretation, actual report writing and the final save are all explicitly separated before assigning zero saving.

s1 is the ordinary case and readiness check for the actual examination, not a new approval ceremony. Changes to authority, case or examination scope require renewed checks. No new examination method or generated clinical instruction.
Existing case templates, recording tools and any dictation are already baseline; no new manual transcription burden is invented. The same-system save is negligible and fully retained.
No report distribution, death registration or statutory filing is silently carried out or removed. If part of the actual episode, its final-version check and separate gated send must be added.
All 100 focal effort points remain. Gross and net saving are zero; incremental work is explicitly zero because no change is proposed.
research_questions: Does observation establish any manual administrative transfer beyond the current native case tools?

already_counted.description: Actual case/readiness verification and substantive report writing and final checking

incremental.description: No new process or software to maintain

approvals.approved_version: Specific autopsy case, authority and readiness checked in s1; changed case or scope requires recheck
Exact complete autopsy record checked in s4; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Actual physical work, evidence capture, causal reasoning and report writing/checking remain; negligible save earns no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct antibody tests and diagnose infections

steps.what: Verify actual patient and specimen context and check the exact ordered antibody test and established laboratory procedure
inputs: Actual test order and clinical context
Specimen identity and established laboratory procedure in the pathology information system, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Checked case, ordered test and readiness for the specific test or a hold

steps.what: Conduct the actual tests to detect antibodies using the established procedure and capture and verify the resulting evidence
inputs: Exact ordered test and readiness checked in s1
Existing laboratory instruments, defined as OTHER
outputs: Actual captured test results and quality limitations

steps.what: Interpret the actual antibody evidence and diagnose infections with appropriate attention to clinical context and uncertainty
inputs: Actual test evidence from s2
Verified clinical context
outputs: Pathologist's diagnostic interpretation and limitations

steps.what: Write the actual diagnostic record and check its complete clinical wording, source results and identifiers
inputs: Actual diagnostic interpretation and source evidence
outputs: Complete checked diagnostic record

steps.what: Save the exact checked diagnostic record
inputs: Exact complete record from s4
outputs: Saved diagnostic record with actual review status

tasks.design: Configure fixed case-identifier fields in the existing {OPS_SYSTEM} diagnostic record. The pathologist retains testing, evidence capture, diagnosis and substantive writing and checks the complete final record before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some record forms may still require repeated case-identifier entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case-linked forms can reuse confirmed identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Test validity and clinical interpretation require professional judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise limitations and integrate findings with the actual clinical context.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native case-linked record fields can reduce repeated identifiers without performing antibody testing or diagnosing infection.

assumptions: Conditional focal-role testing episode with an actual diagnostic record; no measured baseline or claim that the pathologist personally performs every laboratory test.

Case/order owners produce existing records. Pathologist verification is counted in s1 and actual test evidence capture in s2. If laboratory personnel perform testing, represent their labour separately before recalculating; do not eliminate or hide it.

Native forms first; existing instrument automation, assay runtime, result imports and case-linked fields are baseline. Only demonstrated repeated identifier entry in s4 supports a reduction; no hidden new result-import saving.

s1 checks the actual final ordered test and established procedure before s2. Changed test or case requires a renewed check. No new test method, parameter, generated diagnosis, treatment or automatic order.

All clinical writing and complete final checking remain in s4. Save is negligible and fully retained; any report release requires its own final-version gate and separate send. Deduplicate with 17191 if the same report.
All 100 illustrative focal points: gross 1.4 less upkeep 0.5 gives net 0.9; zero if native identifier fields already exist.
unknowns: Actual allocation of testing labour and remaining identifier entry
research_questions: Is there any repeated case-identifier entry left after native laboratory integration?

already_counted.description: Case verification and retained actual diagnostic writing and final checking

incremental.description: Maintain and validate fixed case fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact actual case and ordered test checked in s1; changes require recheck
Exact complete diagnostic record checked in s4; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional fixed-identifier saving 1.4 minus upkeep 0.5; all testing and clinical interpretation retained.

tasks.short: Conduct DNA or chromosome analyses for biopsy and cell diagnosis

steps.what: Verify the actual biopsy or cell-sample identity, clinical question and exact ordered genetic analysis under the established laboratory procedure
inputs: Actual biopsy or cell sample and order
Existing case context and established procedure in the pathology information system, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Checked case, analysis scope and readiness or a hold

steps.what: Conduct the actual genetic analyses of DNA or chromosomes using established methods and capture and verify the resulting evidence
inputs: Exact analysis and readiness checked in s1
Existing genetic-analysis instruments and software, defined as OTHER
outputs: Actual captured analysis results and quality limitations

steps.what: Interpret the actual DNA or chromosome evidence to diagnose the biopsy or cell sample and state unresolved findings
inputs: Actual analysis evidence from s2
Verified sample and clinical context
outputs: Pathologist's diagnostic interpretation and limitations

steps.what: Write the actual genetic-analysis diagnostic record and check its complete findings, sample identifiers and source references
inputs: Actual clinical interpretation and source evidence
outputs: Complete checked genetic-analysis record

steps.what: Save the exact checked genetic-analysis diagnostic record
inputs: Exact complete record from s4
outputs: Saved analysis interpretation with actual review status

tasks.design: Configure native fixed sample and case fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The pathologist retains the genetic analyses, evidence checking, diagnostic interpretation and actual report writing, checking the complete final record before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some case forms may repeat sample and case identifiers already confirmed elsewhere.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case-linked fields can reuse those exact identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Analysis quality and diagnostic significance require specialist interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Integrate genetic evidence and morphology and recognise uncertain findings.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native case-linked forms can reuse exact specimen identifiers while genetic-analysis interpretation remains expert work.

assumptions: Conditional episode with actual focal-role genetic-analysis work and an existing diagnostic record, not a measured baseline. Actual labour allocation must be observed before generalizing to teams where technicians conduct the analyses.
Existing case sources are produced by their owners; pathologist verification is counted in s1 and actual analysis evidence capture in s2. No free new structured analysis feed.

Native fields first; existing analysis software, pipelines, unattended runtime and result imports are baseline and earn no new saving. s4 reduces only demonstrated identifier entry, with substantive writing and the complete final check retained.

s1 checks the actual ordered analysis and established procedure before s2; changed case or analysis requires renewed checking. No new protocol, variant classifier, model diagnosis or automatic test order.

Saving is negligible and fully retained. Actual report distribution, if required, must have its own final-version check and separate send; none is silently performed. Deduplicate shared case and report work with 17187 or 17191.
All 100 illustrative focal points: gross 1.4 less upkeep 0.5 gives net 0.9; existing equivalent native fields yield zero.
unknowns: Current analysis workflow and actual remaining repeated identifier entry
research_questions: Does any manual case-field entry remain after current pathology and genetic-analysis systems?

incremental.description: Maintain and validate native case and sample fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact case and ordered genetic analysis checked in s1; changes require recheck
Exact complete genetic-analysis record checked in s4; edits require recheck
